_source: Nguyen, Srndic & Neth, Noise Contrastive Estimation-based Matching Framework for Low-Resource Security Attack Pattern Recognition, Findings EACL 2024, https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-eacl.25/. Task framing from the abstract (p. 355): 'Identifying TTPs in cybersecurity writing, often called TTP mapping'. The yes/no question is the paper's own zero-shot LLM prompt (App. D.3, p. 369: 'What MITRE ATT&CK techniques (TTPs) are explicitly and implicitly mentioned in the following text: [..]') asked once per candidate TTP, mirroring the paper's pointwise matcher g(x, y) that scores the input text against each TTP's textual profile (Sections 3-4.1; Section 5.3: 'The rich textual description of a TTP is selected for the textual profile'). {id} = ATT&CK ID; {name} = MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v12.0 name (the paper's ATT&CK version, App. A), 'Parent: Sub-technique' for sub-techniques; {description} = the released textual profile from ttp-desc-mappings.csv, verbatim (lower-cased, markup-stripped v12.0 description as released by the authors). The candidate inventory is data/frozen/ttp/candidates.jsonl, pinned by _candidates_sha256. Deprecated/revoked status and tactics are not shown (the paper's matcher sees only the textual profile).
_primitive: noul (one per candidate TTP; all 737 candidates for every text; rank by P(yes))
